data_status: STRICT MODE: this dataset contains only values that were compared with, or ingested directly from, retrieved sources: JPL (SSD, SBDB, NHATS), NASA (NSSDC fact sheets and mission catalog, Small Spacecraft SoA report 2026, SLS page, Apollo 11 press kit, NTRS papers, data.nasa.gov), ULA, ESA, NIST, and the Launch Library 2 aggregator. Records carry source_authority/confidence where the source is an aggregator or vendor-reported compilation. Recalled, estimated and fictional values (optimizer catalog, costs, engine/vehicle specs without a retrievable source, the user-supplied SpaceX table) are not included. Derived values are computed only from verified inputs and are labelled derived.

record.name: Infrared Interferometer Spectrometer (IRIS)
record.description: This investigation was carried out using a Michelson interferometer and a single-channel radiometer similar in design to the Mariner 9 IRIS, combined into a single instrument. The investigation studied both global and local energy balance. Atmospheric composition was also investigated, including determination of the H2/He ratio, and the abundance of CH2 and NH3. Vertical temperature profiles were obtained on the planets and satellites with atmospheres. Studies of the composition, thermal properties, and size of particles in Saturn's rings were conducted. The interferometer had a spectral range of approximately 180 to 2500 1/cm (4-55 micrometers), while the radiometer range covered the spectra from approximately 5000 to 30000 1/cm (0.33-2 micrometers). The nominal apodized spectral resolution of the interferometer was 4.3 1/cm. The instruments shared a half-meter Cassegrain telescope with a 0.25-deg field of view. The basic quantity measured was the spectral radiance of emitted and reflected IR radiation and a large fraction of reflected visible energy. The interferometer was calibrated using deep space (assumed to be a black body at 0 deg K) and the internal instrument temperature as reference points. The radiometer was calibrated with a diffuser plate of known radiometric properties. For a description of the instrument see Hanel, R. et al., 1977, Applied Optics, v. 19, p. 1391.
